facts.text: Eureka Springs was originally called "The Magic City" and later the "Stairstep Town" because of its winding streets.
The historic downtown preserves a cohesive streetscape of well‑preserved Victorian buildings that attract visitors year‑round.
Since 1968, the Great Passion Play has staged an outdoor drama each summer, drawing a cast of about 170 actors and live animals.
Inspiration Point hosts an annual summer opera festival that began in 1950, making it one of the oldest opera venues in the Ozarks.
Carrie Nation, the temperance activist, founded Hatchet Hall on Steele Street in the late 19th century, a landmark still standing today.
The town’s healing springs, first noted by the Osage Nation, became famous in the late 1800s and helped establish Eureka Springs as a health resort.
